clue.text: Presidential enthusiasm can set the country alight

parts.note: George Bush and George W Bush were US presidents, so the presidential name gives BUSH
fire is ardour or passion, a synonym for enthusiasm

explanation.surface: A president's fervour could inflame the whole nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country' here means the bush, the wild open country of Australia, and the definition describes what the answer does rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire raging through scrubland in the outback is exactly what sets wide stretches of countryside ablaze.

clue.text: Cook for trains on first-class Chunnel link route

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway that ran the trains
A1 means first-class, written here with the letter I standing for the figure one
the Channel Tunnel rail link runs through the South-East of England, abbreviated SE

explanation.surface: A recipe of sorts for a rail route to the Channel Tunnel.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chunnel is the Channel Tunnel between England and France; its link route runs through Kent, in the South-East.
explanation.definitionFit: To stew meat slowly in a covered pot with a little liquid is a way to cook it.

clue.text: Sarah gets depressed and rather jaundiced

parts.note: Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah
low means sad or downcast, as depressed does

explanation.surface: Sarah is feeling down and looking a bit off-colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickly yellowish complexion is what a jaundiced look suggests.

clue.text: Loud pop music becomes a habit

parts.note: f, forte, is the musical marking for loud
rock is a kind of popular music

explanation.surface: Noisy rock music turns into a regular addiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' looks like a custom, but it is the garment, as in a monk's or nun's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A monk's long robe is called both a habit and a frock.

clue.text: Standing for election and apparently canvassing enthusiastically

definitions.meaning: a candidate in an election is said to be in the race for office
a keen canvasser seems to be dashing from door to door at speed

explanation.surface: A candidate in the election seems to be campaigning hard.
explanation.definitionFit: Being a candidate for office and moving at a sprint share the same participle of the verb for going fast.

clue.text: Rex is taken in by a girl? What a jerk!

indicators.note: the girl's letters take in, or contain, the abbreviation for Rex

parts.note: wench is an old word for a girl or young woman
R is the abbreviation for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king is deceived by a young woman, and someone exclaims at the fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerk' seems to be an insult, but it means a sudden sharp pull.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden violent twist or tug is a jerk.

clue.text: Looking about

definitions.meaning: gazing at or eyeing something attentively
concerning or on the subject of, as a preposition

explanation.definitionFit: The participle means gazing at, and the preposition means concerning, both from the verb to regard.

clue.text: Late arriving in Scotland-around midday

indicators.note: in Scots dialect the word no is used for not, so the negative word is swapped for its Scottish form

parts.note: someone who arrives late is not on time

explanation.surface: A train running late in Scotland gets in at about twelve o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scotland 'not' is said 'no', so 'not on time' becomes 'no on time'; run together these letters give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noon is twelve o'clock, so the time of day at noon is around midday.

clue.text: Argued, and with great fluency

definitions.meaning: quarrelled or exchanged angry remarks
read literally, someone who speaks fluently possessed plenty of vocabulary

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for quarrelling, read literally, describes someone who possessed a ready vocabulary.

clue.text: Full board with nobody missing

definitions.meaning: lodging with meals and everything provided, an old term in job adverts for servants
every person searched for has been located

explanation.definitionFit: The old phrase for wages with food and lodging thrown in, read literally, says every person has been located.

clue.text: A prized metal found around the east from prehistoric times

indicators.note: the precious metal goes around the abbreviation for east, enclosing it

parts.note: gold is the most prized of metals

explanation.surface: Treasure dug up with an easterly bearing dates back to the dawn of history.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ancient, dating back for countless years, is from prehistoric times.

clue.text: What the conductor should do best

definitions.meaning: an orchestra's conductor marks the time with a baton
to defeat or outdo, as a verb

explanation.definitionFit: A conductor keeps time with the baton, and to outdo a rival is to defeat them.

clue.text: Keep sealer in the standard packet

parts.note: to stock goods is to keep them for sale
size is a gluey wash used to seal plaster or paper before painting

explanation.surface: A shop keeps decorators' sealant in ordinary-sized packs.
explanation.walkthrough: Size is a thin glue painted on walls to seal them before papering.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods made in regular measurements kept on the shelves are the standard packet a shop carries.

clue.text: Scale a trio adapted

indicators.note: something adapted has been altered, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Music for three players is rearranged to a different scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A proportion between two quantities, as on a map, is its scale.

clue.text: Sell leather

definitions.meaning: British slang for selling something, often by hard pushing
to beat or thrash, as with a leather strap

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for hawking goods, and a verb for thrashing someone with a whip.

clue.text: Hurry to give the appearance of cleverness

definitions.meaning: an order to be quick about it
read literally, to seem bright and quick-witted

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom urging speed, read literally, means to seem keen-witted.

clue.text: Endeavoured to get about a couple of metres cut

indicators.note: the attempt goes about, or around, the two metres

parts.note: tried means attempted, as endeavoured does
M is the abbreviation for metre, so two of them make MM

explanation.surface: Someone attempts to shorten something by two metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or hedges neatly shortened have been clipped back.

clue.text: No chance to work up a dance

indicators.note: working the letters up stirs them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: There is no prospect of getting a dance going.
explanation.definitionFit: A stately Baroque piece in triple time, originally a Spanish dance, is a dance form.

clue.text: Mini auto as opposed to an automobile

definitions.meaning: the Mini is a famous tiny British motor

definitions.text: auto as opposed to an automobile
definitions.meaning: the word auto is a shortened, smaller version of automobile

explanation.definitionFit: The Mini is a compact motor, and auto is the shortened form of automobile.

clue.text: Guy goes to village in which Jack retired

indicators.note: the ridicule goes to, joining on after, the village

parts.note: ham is an old word for a village, seen in place names
to guy someone is to ridicule them, to mock

explanation.surface: A man heads off to a village where a fellow called Jack retired.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or Jack tar, is a sailor, and 'retired' means went to bed: sailors slept in hanging canvas beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Sailors aboard ship traditionally slept slung in a hanging canvas bed.

clue.text: One hears of the old king who reunited Germany

indicators.note: a listener hears the name of the nursery-rhyme monarch, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old king of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: Someone hears a tale of an ancient monarch who united German lands again.
explanation.walkthrough: Helmut Kohl was the German chancellor who oversaw reunification in 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: Helmut Kohl led West Germany into reunification with East Germany in 1990.

clue.text: Books once worn out in Oxford

definitions.meaning: reserves or claims, as in booking a seat
Oxford ... were very wide trousers fashionable in the 1920s

explanation.definitionFit: Children's slang for claiming first, and the wide 1920s trousers called Oxford bags.

clue.text: Total sum no one raised-except maybe the chancellor

definitions.text: Total sum no one raised-except maybe the chancellor

parts.note: a bill is the total sum owed

indicators.note: in a down clue the words no and one are raised, read upward, so their letters run backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Only the finance minister could raise such an enormous sum of money.
explanation.walkthrough: The chancellor is Britain's finance minister; the whole clue describes a sum so vast only government could raise it.
explanation.definitionFit: A thousand million pounds is a sum only a finance minister could raise.

clue.text: Travel in refurbished boat to South American capital

indicators.note: the travel word sits in the middle of the rearranged boat
a refurbished vessel has been redone, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: go means travel or proceed

explanation.surface: Sailing in a renovated vessel to a South American city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Colombia sits high in the Andes.

clue.text: Herb Hutton returned to the marsh

parts.note: a fen is a low marshy area, as in the Fens of eastern England

indicators.note: the cricketer's first name is returned, read back to front

parts.note: Len Hutton was a great English cricketer of the 1930s to 1950s

explanation.surface: A man called Herb Hutton came back to the wetlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Len Hutton was a famous England batsman and captain.
explanation.definitionFit: An aniseed-flavoured plant with feathery leaves used in cooking is a herb.

clue.text: Ponies pass by a back street

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass

indicators.note: the street abbreviation goes back, reading right to left

explanation.surface: Horses trot past a quiet backstreet.
explanation.definitionFit: Young male horses are often called ponies loosely, both being young equines.

clue.text: Good heavens! The incense is burning

definitions.meaning: an exclamation of surprise
read literally, the sacred fumes rising from incense in church

explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation of astonishment that, read literally, describes the sacred fumes from a censer.

clue.text: Footsie generally included investment

indicators.note: the answer is included within the run of letters across these two words

explanation.surface: The FTSE share index usually contains some investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Investment' looks financial beside Footsie (the FTSE 100 share index), but it is the military sense: surrounding a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Investing a fortress means surrounding it with troops, the old military sense of blockade.

clue.text: Cretan squash makes a lovely drink

indicators.note: squashing the word crushes its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A man from Crete makes a delicious fruit cordial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squash' looks like a fruit drink, sitting near 'drink', but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The drink of the gods in Greek myth, or a sweet fruit juice, is a lovely drink.

clue.text: Overcome the stigma of being a basement tenant

definitions.meaning: to get over the shame of a past mistake
read literally, someone who resides on the bottom floor

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for outgrowing a disgrace, read literally, means residing below ground level.

clue.text: A continent and pure old English composition

indicators.note: a composition is something put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An essay in plain old English about a landmass.
explanation.definitionFit: The landmass west of Asia is one of the world's seven continents.

clue.text: Let India be prepared with all the facts

indicators.note: the letters are prepared, made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: India should be given the full briefing so it can get ready.
explanation.definitionFit: Explaining something thoroughly, point by point, covers all the facts.
